findings.summary: Runtime proofpack schema/signum metadata is checked against the plugin/schema sources and docs examples.
findings.remainingRisk: Future metadata edits must keep the static guard passing.

findings.summary: DSL exec steps validate argv and run with bounded timeout handling.
findings.remainingRisk: Timeout behavior is only as deterministic as the local process and OS scheduler.

findings.summary: PR CI runs the deterministic shell test suite, including clean-room smoke via tests/test-cleanroom-smoke.sh, without secrets, AI CLIs, or writable contents permission.
findings.remainingRisk: CI host image contents remain external to the repository.

findings.summary: Project root resolution no longer relies on unsafe home-directory scans and is statically guarded.
findings.remainingRisk: Users can still pass an explicit project root that points to the wrong project.

findings.summary: Generated Signum gate workflows install Claude Code CLI from a pinned version file instead of a floating package spec.
findings.remainingRisk: npm package resolution and transitive runtime contents are not fully vendored.

findings.summary: The release workflow still pushes to Emporium on the write path, but preflight checks, dry-run mode, repository guard, secret gating, and clean-room local smoke bound the risk.
findings.remainingRisk: A successful non-dry-run release can still mutate a separate repository.

findings.summary: Root .signum artifact usage is inventoried and normal runtime artifacts are documented as canonical under .signum/contracts/<contractId>/.
findings.remainingRisk: Explicit legacy import/cleanup compatibility remains until a future removal decision.

findings.summary: Normal-runtime legacy helper call sites were migrated to canonical-only helpers and remaining legacy calls are allowlisted by category.
findings.remainingRisk: Legacy resume/import/archive/close compatibility paths still exist by design.

findings.summary: Proofpack validation checks required fields, metadata drift, envelopes, artifact refs, and optional removalEvidence shape.
findings.remainingRisk: The validator is focused code, not a general JSON Schema engine.

findings.summary: Policy rules have stable ruleId values, a catalog contract, fixture references, and mirrored root/platform coverage.
findings.remainingRisk: New rules must be added through the catalog and fixture contract.

findings.summary: RuleId suppressions and dependency file-scope reduce known false positives while preserving regex scanner behavior.
findings.remainingRisk: Regex matching can still miss or over-match language semantics.

findings.summary: Large init harness markdown heredocs are extracted into checked-in templates with golden scaffold coverage.
findings.remainingRisk: Template edits must update golden fixtures intentionally.

findings.summary: The scanner implementation is Python stdlib with a thin shell compatibility wrapper and golden behavior fixtures.
findings.remainingRisk: The scanner remains heuristic and emits large text signals.

findings.summary: The command is still large, but command structure, renderer output, and fragment parity are now guarded before deeper decomposition.
findings.remainingRisk: Full semantic refactor is not done.

findings.summary: Root/Claude overlay differences are documented as bounded deviations, including overlay-only RECONCILE.
findings.remainingRisk: New overlay differences must be classified instead of silently drifting.

findings.summary: External GitHub Actions uses refs are pinned to full commit SHAs and recorded in a static inventory.
findings.remainingRisk: Action source repositories and GitHub execution infrastructure remain external.

findings.summary: Scanned GitHub-hosted runner labels use fixed ubuntu-24.04 labels instead of ubuntu-latest.
findings.remainingRisk: Fixed labels do not freeze image patch contents.

findings.summary: removalEvidence remains optional and root-only; absence is valid and presence is shape-validated.
findings.remainingRisk: Overlay cleanup obligations are represented later through RECONCILE rather than root-style removalEvidence.

findings.summary: Root Final Output keeps exactly three cleanup-only purge_root_working_set_views calls; overlay has no matching Step 4.5 flow.
findings.remainingRisk: The root-only Final Output flow remains a documented compatibility exception.

findings.summary: The repository does not fully freeze runner images, OS package contents, or all toolchain transitive inputs.
findings.remainingRisk: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 images can still receive patch updates.

findings.summary: go.sum is still not captured as an init scanner manifest signal.
findings.remainingRisk: Go dependency lockfile signal can be absent from init context.

findings.summary: Optional reviewer/provider availability remains dependent on external CLI auth, version compatibility, and network state.
findings.remainingRisk: External reviewers can be unavailable even when local deterministic guards pass.

findings.summary: Further semantic command decomposition or parameterized fragments can be considered after the current renderer/parity baseline remains stable.
findings.remainingRisk: Large command fragments still require careful review.

findings.summary: Parser-aware policy scanning could reduce regex false positives and false negatives for high-value languages.
findings.remainingRisk: Any parser work must preserve current ruleId and suppression contracts.

findings.summary: A clean CI release/package dry-run can further validate the hardened release path before publishing.
findings.remainingRisk: Local/static tests do not prove full release environment behavior.

findings.summary: An explicit enterprise data-egress policy could define when optional external reviewers are allowed or disabled.
findings.remainingRisk: Current documentation describes local artifacts and optional providers but does not define a full enterprise policy.
